title: Is This a Valid Tree Network?
statement: You are given n nodes labeled 0 to n-1 and a list of undirected edges, each edge a list [u, v]. Return True if these edges form a valid tree (the graph is connected and contains no cycles), and False otherwise.
hints: A valid tree on n nodes must be both fully connected and cycle-free; checking these two properties together is a classic union-find application.
A graph with n nodes is a tree if and only if it has exactly n-1 edges AND no cycle forms while adding them (equivalently, after adding all edges there is exactly one connected component).

First check edge count equals n-1 (fail fast otherwise); then union each edge's endpoints, returning False immediately if an edge connects two nodes already sharing a root, and True if you finish with a single component.
